gen-dafont-redux-noto-serif: Redux spreads its wide-set letters out, each curve taking a big visible run-up on entry. And Noto Serif follows with a prominent x-height and a faint thick-and-thin rhythm, a text serif that grounds all that space.
gen-dafont-riesling-fs-sentient: Dense black stems, hairline serifs, vintage to the bone. Sentient takes over with a classic serif's pinched apertures and crossbars a touch thinner than the stems, so Riesling gets the loud part and nothing competes.
gen-dafont-sf-wonder-comic-fs-gambetta: Tall, dense, a little cartoon-sturdy: SF Wonder Comic leaves its bowls open on one side. Gambetta settles in below as a text serif with wide channels into every counter, and its lowercase sits lower, which gives the heading room to stand up.
gen-dafont-sf-wonder-comic-lora: Lora brings a broad, welcoming c and only modest hairline thinning at its curves. Beneath SF Wonder Comic's tall, dense heading, its moderate lowercase height lets a text serif unwind slowly, bookish and unhurried.
gen-dafont-sophia-bitter: Pen-written flow up top, sturdy slab below. Bitter's very large lowercase and see-through s keep a long page of text feeling grounded, while Sophia's open curves float over it.
gen-dafont-sophia-inter: Sophia's flowing, pen-written strokes come first, tall and loose. Inter follows as a plain sans with big counters and a smooth, tube-like line, and if the heading shrinks too far, its hand-drawn character would fade.
gen-dafont-sophia-mulish: Loose pen strokes meet a smooth, uniform line. Mulish works with Sophia by dropping thick-and-thin altogether, using a large x-height and horseshoe-open apertures, so the sans stays quiet while the script moves.
gen-dafont-sophia-roboto-slab: Sophia writes in tall, flowing curves with open mouths. Roboto Slab, a slab-serif with a dominant middle zone and open throats in a, c, e and s, gives a long page a precise, structured texture.
gen-dafont-sophia-rubik: Rubik's lowercase looks big beside its capitals, with round, open shapes. Sophia's script has no hairlines and no swells, so the two sit together smoothly, one flowing and one soft.
gen-dafont-starborn-fs-gambetta: Dreamy, with big stretches of blank space between the letters. Gambetta, a classic serif with wide channels into each counter and weight that shifts only slightly, handles the steady reading that Starborn's dark, spacious stripe leaves alone.
